instructions:
# SAST + DAST

Layered application security: static analysis in CI, dynamic testing against running apps.

## What This Skill Does

- Runs language-specific SAST scanners (bandit, gosec, eslint)
- Scans IaC and dependencies in the same pipeline
- Executes OWASP ZAP baseline and full scans against environments
- Correlates findings into a single remediation report

## When to Use

- Pre-release security gate for web applications
- API security review with OpenAPI-driven ZAP scans
- Investigating a suspected app-level vulnerability

## Real Commands

```bash
# SAST
bandit -r src/ -f json -o bandit.json
semgrep scan --config p/owasp-top-ten .
trivy fs --scanners vuln,secret,config .
gosec ./...

# DAST against staging
zap-baseline.py -t https://staging.example.com -r report.html
zap-full-scan.py -t https://staging.example.com -J zap.json
nikto -h https://staging.example.com
nuclei -u https://staging.example.com -severity high,critical
zap-api-scan.py -t https://staging.example.com/swagger.json -f openapi
```

## Pipeline Shape

```yaml
stages:
  sast:
    - bandit -r src/ && semgrep scan --config auto .
  deps:
    - trivy fs --scanners vuln,secret,config .
  dast:
    - zap-baseline.py -t $STAGING_URL -r report.html
```

## Best Practices

- Run SAST on every PR; DAST on staging after deploy
- Use ZAP's API scan against the OpenAPI spec to hit every endpoint
- De-duplicate by CWE across tools
- Gate deploys on critical SAST; use DAST as release evidence
- Protect staging environments with auth tokens in ZAP scans
